title: Apply for a new PAN card
summary: A PAN card is used for tax and many financial records in India. This guide explains the basic application flow and the points a user should confirm on the official PAN portal before submitting.
documents_needed: Recent photograph if required by the selected application flow

steps.title: Open an official PAN application portal
steps.detail: Use the official Protean/NSDL or UTIITSL PAN service. Avoid agent websites unless you deliberately choose paid help.

steps.title: Choose the correct application type
steps.detail: Select the option for a new PAN and the applicant category that matches the user, such as individual Indian citizen.

steps.title: Enter details consistently
steps.detail: Names, date of birth, and address should match the supporting documents. Mismatches can cause rejection or delay.

steps.title: Submit identity and address documents
steps.detail: Upload or provide documents using the method supported by the official portal. Keep scans clear and readable.

steps.title: Pay only through the official payment flow
steps.detail: Check the current official fee on the portal before payment because fees and delivery options can change.

steps.title: Save the acknowledgement
steps.detail: Keep the acknowledgement number or receipt so the application can be tracked later.

warnings.title: Confirm the latest official form and fee
warnings.message: PAN application forms, portals, and fees can change. Confirm the latest requirement on the official portal before submitting.

warnings.title: Avoid sharing real ID data in the demo
warnings.message: During project development, use only fake examples. Do not upload real PAN, Aadhaar, address, or bank details.

title: File your Income Tax Return (ITR) - basics
summary: Income Tax Return filing is done through the Income Tax Department e-filing portal. This guide explains the basic user flow and reminds users to confirm the current assessment year, form, deadline, and e-verification rules on the official portal.
documents_needed: Form 16 for salaried users if available
Investment and deduction proofs if claiming deductions

steps.title: Open the Income Tax e-filing portal
steps.detail: Use the official Income Tax Department portal and sign in with the correct taxpayer account.

steps.title: Choose the correct assessment year and form
steps.detail: The form depends on the user's income type and situation. A salaried person may often use ITR-1, but this must be confirmed.

steps.title: Review pre-filled information
steps.detail: Check income, tax deducted, bank details, and deductions. Do not assume pre-filled data is always complete.

steps.title: Submit and e-verify
steps.detail: Submission is not the end of the process. The return must also be verified using an allowed method.

steps.title: Save acknowledgement
steps.detail: Download the acknowledgement or ITR-V and keep it for records.

warnings.title: Deadline changes must be checked live
warnings.message: Filing deadlines can be extended or changed. Confirm the current deadline on the official Income Tax portal before relying on any date.

warnings.title: E-verification is required
warnings.message: If a filed return is not verified within the required time, it may not be treated as valid. Confirm the current rule on the official portal.

title: Understand a loan agreement
summary: A loan agreement explains the borrower, lender, amount, interest rate, repayment schedule, fees, default consequences, and complaint process. This guide helps users identify clauses worth checking before signing or asking a bank officer.

steps.title: Check amount, tenure, and interest type
steps.detail: Confirm the principal amount, loan duration, and whether the rate is fixed, floating, or mixed.

steps.title: Read the EMI schedule
steps.detail: Confirm the EMI amount, due date, number of instalments, and total repayment amount.

steps.title: Find penalty and default clauses
steps.detail: Look for late payment charges, penal charges, and consequences of default. Ask the lender to explain exact amounts and triggers.

steps.title: Check prepayment and foreclosure terms
steps.detail: Some loans have restrictions or charges for early repayment. Rules differ by loan type, lender type, and rate type.

steps.title: List all fees and add-ons
steps.detail: Processing fees, documentation charges, insurance, and other add-ons should be clear before signing.

steps.title: Find the complaint process
steps.detail: The agreement or lender website should explain how to raise complaints and escalate unresolved issues.

warnings.title: Late payment and penal charges
warnings.message: Penalty terms can significantly increase cost. Ask when the charge applies, how it is calculated, and whether taxes or extra charges apply.

warnings.title: Prepayment and foreclosure conditions
warnings.message: Do not assume early repayment is free. Check the exact clause and ask the lender how it applies to this loan type.

warnings.title: Bundled products
warnings.message: If insurance or other products are bundled with the loan, ask whether they are optional and how they affect total cost.

source.name: Reserve Bank of India consumer and fair practices materials

title: Aadhaar Enrolment Basics
summary: Aadhaar is a 12-digit individual identification number issued by the UIDAI on behalf of the Government of India. First-time enrolment is free of cost. Children under 5 are exempt from biometric capture (only a photograph is taken). This guide explains how to enrol for Aadhaar for the first time.
documents_needed: Proof of Date of Birth (date of birth proof)

steps.title: Locate an Enrolment Center
steps.detail: Find the nearest Aadhaar Enrolment Center authorized by UIDAI. You may optionally book an appointment online at the UIDAI portal to reduce waiting time, but walk-in enrolment is also available at most centers.

steps.title: Visit the Center
steps.detail: Go to the center with your original supporting documents.

steps.title: Provide Biometrics
steps.detail: Your fingerprints, iris scan, and photograph will be captured. Note: Children under 5 years of age are exempt from biometrics (only a photograph is taken). Biometrics are mandatory for all others.

steps.title: Collect Acknowledgment
steps.detail: Keep the enrolment slip containing the Enrolment ID (EID) to track status.

warnings.title: Free of Cost
warnings.message: First-time Aadhaar enrolment is completely free of cost. Do not pay any fees at the enrolment center.

warnings.title: Children Under 5 - Biometric Exemption
warnings.message: Children below 5 years are exempt from biometric capture (fingerprints and iris scan). Only a facial photograph is taken. Aadhaar must be updated with biometrics when the child turns 5 and again at 15.

title: Link PAN with Aadhaar
summary: The government mandates linking your PAN with Aadhaar. Failure to link makes the PAN inoperative, restricting financial transactions.

steps.title: Visit the Income Tax e-Filing Portal
steps.detail: Go to the official e-filing portal and find the 'Link Aadhaar' option.

steps.title: Enter Details
steps.detail: Provide your PAN, Aadhaar number, and Name as per Aadhaar.

steps.title: Pay Penalty if Applicable
steps.detail: If linking after the deadline, a late fee may apply. Pay it via the e-Pay Tax functionality.

steps.title: Verify via OTP
steps.detail: Enter the OTP received on your Aadhaar-linked mobile number to complete the request.

warnings.title: Inoperative PAN Consequences
warnings.message: An inoperative PAN prevents filing ITR, opens you to higher TDS, and restricts bank accounts.

title: EPF Withdrawal Process
summary: The Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) allows partial or full withdrawal under specific conditions such as unemployment, medical emergencies, or retirement.

steps.title: Activate UAN
steps.detail: Ensure your UAN is activated and your KYC details (Aadhaar, PAN, Bank) are verified.

steps.title: Log in to Member Portal
steps.detail: Visit the EPFO unified member portal and sign in with UAN and password.

steps.title: Select Claim Form
steps.detail: Go to Online Services and choose 'Claim (Form-31, 19, 10C & 10D)'.

steps.title: Verify Bank Account
steps.detail: Enter the last 4 digits of your registered bank account to verify.

steps.title: Submit Request
steps.detail: Choose the type of withdrawal, upload a scanned cheque if required, and submit with Aadhaar OTP.

warnings.title: Tax Implications
warnings.message: Withdrawing EPF before 5 years of continuous service may attract TDS.

title: Filing a First Information Report (FIR)
summary: An FIR is a written document prepared by the police when they receive information about the commission of a cognizable offence.

steps.title: Visit the Police Station
steps.detail: Go to the police station having jurisdiction over the area where the crime occurred.

steps.title: Narrate the Incident
steps.detail: Provide details of the incident orally or submit a written complaint.

steps.title: Sign the FIR
steps.detail: The police will write down oral information. Read it carefully and sign it.

steps.title: Get a Copy
steps.detail: You have the right to get a copy of the FIR free of cost.

warnings.title: Zero FIR
warnings.message: If you are away from the jurisdiction, you can file a 'Zero FIR' at any police station, which will later be transferred to the correct one.

warnings.title: False Information
warnings.message: Providing false information to the police is a punishable offence.

title: Opening a Savings Bank Account
summary: A savings account keeps your money safe while earning modest interest. RBI mandates banks to follow KYC norms for all new accounts.
documents_needed: Valid KYC Document (Aadhaar, Passport, Voter ID, etc.)

steps.title: Choose a Bank
steps.detail: Select a bank based on interest rates, minimum balance requirements, and branch proximity.

steps.title: Fill the Application Form
steps.detail: Visit the branch or apply online through the bank's portal.

steps.title: Submit KYC Documents
steps.detail: Provide Proof of Identity and Proof of Address. Video KYC is also available for many banks.

steps.title: Make Initial Deposit
steps.detail: Deposit the required minimum balance amount if applicable.

steps.title: Collect Starter Kit
steps.detail: Receive your passbook, cheque book, and debit card.

warnings.title: Minimum Balance Penalties
warnings.message: Be aware of the Minimum Average Balance (MAB) requirements. Failing to maintain it can result in monthly penalties.

title: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana
summary: PM-KISAN provides income support of Rs. 6,000 per year to landholding farmer families across the country.

steps.title: Check Eligibility
steps.detail: Ensure you own cultivable land and do not fall under the exclusion categories (e.g., taxpayers, professionals).

steps.title: Visit PM Kisan Portal
steps.detail: Go to the official PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in).

steps.title: New Farmer Registration
steps.detail: Click on 'New Farmer Registration' under the Farmers Corner.

steps.title: Enter Details
steps.detail: Provide Aadhaar, select your state, and fill out the registration form with land and bank details.

steps.title: Complete e-KYC
steps.detail: e-KYC is mandatory for registered farmers to receive instalments.

warnings.title: Recovery of Funds
warnings.message: If an ineligible person claims the benefit, the government can initiate recovery proceedings.

title: Filing a Consumer Court Complaint
summary: If you have purchased a product or service with defects or deficiencies, you can file a complaint with the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

steps.title: Send a Legal Notice
steps.detail: Before filing, send a formal notice to the seller giving them a chance to resolve the issue.

steps.title: Draft the Complaint
steps.detail: Prepare a formal complaint stating the facts, defect, and relief sought.

steps.title: Choose the Correct Forum
steps.detail: File at District, State, or National level depending on the value of goods/services.

steps.title: Pay the Fee
steps.detail: Pay the nominal court fee via a demand draft or online payment.

steps.title: File Online via e-Daakhil
steps.detail: You can file the complaint electronically through the e-Daakhil portal.

warnings.title: Time Limit
warnings.message: A consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date the cause of action arose.

title: Apply for an Indian Passport (Fresh/Re-issue)
summary: Apply for a fresh Indian passport or re-issue of an existing passport online through the official Passport Seva portal (passportindia.gov.in) under the Ministry of External Affairs. The process involves online registration, filling Form No. 1, paying the fee, scheduling an appointment at a Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) or Post Office PSK (POPSK), biometric capture, document verification, and police verification before final dispatch.
documents_needed: Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate, School Leaving Certificate, Aadhaar Card, or PAN Card)
Proof of Present Address (Aadhaar Card, Water/Electricity Bill, Bank Passbook with Photo, or Rent Agreement)
Proof of Identity with Photo (Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, or PAN Card)
Standard Annexure E declaration (for adult fresh passport applicants)
Non-ECR Proof (10th standard matriculation certificate or higher educational degree, if applicable)

steps.title: Register on the Passport Seva Online Portal
steps.detail: Visit the official portal at passportindia.gov.in and click 'New User Registration'. Select your jurisdictional Passport Office and provide your basic details.

steps.title: Fill out the Passport Application Form
steps.detail: Login with your registered ID, click 'Apply for Fresh Passport/Re-issue of Passport', choose Normal or Tatkaal scheme, select a 36 or 60 page booklet, and complete the form accurately.

steps.title: Pay Application Fee and Schedule Appointment
steps.detail: Go to 'View Saved/Submitted Applications' and click 'Pay and Schedule Appointment'. Pay online (₹1,500 for normal adult 36-page passport) and select your preferred PSK/POPSK and appointment slot.

steps.title: Visit PSK / POPSK for Biometrics and Document Verification
steps.detail: Arrive on the scheduled date with original documents, self-attested photocopies, and application receipt. Complete photograph, fingerprint capture, and document checking.

steps.title: Complete Police Verification and Receive Passport
steps.detail: After your appointment, local police will verify your residential address. Once cleared, your passport is printed and delivered to your doorstep via India Post Speed Post.

warnings.title: Beware of Fraudulent Third-Party Websites
warnings.message: Only apply through the official government portal www.passportindia.gov.in. Avoid fake intermediary sites charging extra fees.

warnings.title: Carry All Original Documents to PSK
warnings.message: You must bring original documents corresponding to every uploaded copy. Missing originals will lead to appointment cancellation and rescheduling.

warnings.title: Ensure Present Residential Address is Accurate
warnings.message: Police verification is strictly carried out at the current address entered in the application. Concealing residential history can lead to penalties under the Passports Act.

source.name: Ministry of External Affairs - Passport Seva Portal

title: Aadhaar PVC Card Payment Deducted but SRN Not Generated
summary: If ₹50 was debited from your bank account or UPI (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm) for an Aadhaar PVC card but no Service Request Number (SRN) or receipt was generated, UIDAI's payment gateway reconciliation takes 24 to 48 hours. If the order is not created, the bank automatically refunds the amount.
documents_needed: Bank account statement or UPI transaction screenshot showing UTR number

steps.title: Wait for the 24-48 Hour Reconciliation Window
steps.detail: Payment gateways communicate status asynchronously. In many cases, the order updates retroactively within 24 to 48 hours.

steps.title: Check Status Online at myAadhaar Portal
steps.detail: Visit myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in, log in with your Aadhaar and OTP, and check the 'Requests' section at the bottom of the dashboard to see if an SRN was assigned.

steps.title: Bank Auto-Reversal Timeline
steps.detail: If the portal did not register the SRN, the amount will be refunded by your bank/payment aggregator back to the source account within 5 to 7 business days.

steps.title: Contact UIDAI Helpdesk if Refund Fails
steps.detail: If the refund does not arrive within 7 days, dial UIDAI toll-free helpline at 1947 or email helpdesk@uidai.gov.in with your 12-digit bank UTR reference number.

warnings.title: Do Not Double-Pay Immediately
warnings.message: Avoid repeatedly attempting payments within the first 2 hours to prevent multiple deductions.

title: Income Tax Bank Account Validation Failed & Refund Unpaid Fix
summary: When an Income Tax refund fails with 'Refund Unpaid' or bank account status shows 'Validation Failed', it is usually due to a name mismatch, merged bank IFSC code changes, or unlinked PAN in core banking.
documents_needed: Latest Bank Passbook or Statement showing correct current IFSC
Valid Mobile Number linked with Bank Account

steps.title: Check Failure Reason in Profile
steps.detail: Log in to incometax.gov.in, navigate to Profile > My Bank Account, and click on the red exclamation mark next to the failed bank account to read the exact error.

steps.title: Update Merged Bank IFSC Code
steps.detail: If your bank underwent a merger (e.g. Syndicate Bank to Canara Bank, Allahabad Bank to Indian Bank), remove the old bank account and re-add it with the new IFSC.

steps.title: Ensure Core Banking Demographic Match
steps.detail: Ensure your name in your bank account matches your PAN card letter-for-letter and that your PAN is actively seeded with the bank branch.

steps.title: Submit Refund Reissue Request
steps.detail: Once your bank account status shows green 'Validated' and 'Nominated for Refund', go to Services > Refund Reissue > Create Refund Reissue Request to release the pending refund.

warnings.title: Refund Will Not Be Processed to Unvalidated Accounts
warnings.message: Income tax refunds can only be credited to pre-validated bank accounts where PAN-bank name matching is verified.

source.name: Income Tax Department e-Filing Helpdesk Manual

title: Passport Police Verification Delayed Past 21 Days or Adverse Report
summary: Under the Ministry of External Affairs Citizen Charter, the standard turnaround time for police verification is 21 calendar days. If verification is stuck beyond 21 days or marked 'Adverse', follow these resolution steps.
documents_needed: Passport Application Receipt (ARN slip) with 15-digit File Number
Original current address proof (Aadhaar, utility bill, or registered rent agreement)

steps.title: Track File Number Online
steps.detail: Visit passportindia.gov.in, click 'Track Application Status', select Passport, and enter your 15-digit File Number and Date of Birth to check the current stage.

steps.title: Visit Local Police Station or LIB Office
steps.detail: If status remains 'Pending' past 21 days, visit the assigned police station or the District Police Headquarters (Local Intelligence Branch / Special Branch) with your documents.

steps.title: Respond Promptly to Adverse Notice
steps.detail: If the report was marked 'Adverse' (such as applicant not found at residence during visit), the Regional Passport Office will send an inquiry letter. Submit a formal clarification within 30 days.

steps.title: Book an RPO Inquiry Appointment
steps.detail: If unassisted, log in to the Passport Seva portal, book an 'Enquiry Appointment' at your jurisdictional Regional Passport Office (RPO), and meet the Passport Officer in person.

warnings.title: Do Not Pay Bribes for Verification
warnings.message: Police verification is an official statutory duty. Never pay unauthorized fees to visiting verification officers; escalate any misconduct to the SP/DCP office.

source.name: Passport Seva Project - Ministry of External Affairs

title: EPF Joint Declaration SOP for Name, Father's Name, and Exit Date Correction
summary: Under EPFO's Joint Declaration Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), demographic and service discrepancies (Member Name, Father's Name, Date of Joining, Date of Exit) can be corrected online through the Member Portal with employer digital signature.
documents_needed: Passport, PAN Card, or Birth Certificate (as secondary proof)
Employer Appointment Letter or Relieving Letter (for date of joining/exit errors)

steps.title: Log in to Member Unified Portal
steps.detail: Visit unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in, log in with your UAN and password, and navigate to Manage > Joint Declaration.

steps.title: Select Member ID & Fill Correct Details
steps.detail: Choose the establishment member ID. Enter the correct detail (Name, DOB, Gender, Father Name, Date of Joining, or Date of Exit) exactly as per Aadhaar.

steps.title: Upload Required Supporting Proofs
steps.detail: Upload PDF copies of supporting documents as specified under EPFO's Joint Declaration SOP Table A.

steps.title: Employer Approval & EPFO Verification
steps.detail: Submit the request. Your employer must review and digitally sign the request via their Employer Portal, after which the EPFO Field Office processes the change.

warnings.title: Employer Digital Signature Mandatory
warnings.message: Online Joint Declaration requests cannot proceed without your employer's DSC approval on the EPFO portal.

source.name: EPFO Joint Declaration Standard Operating Procedure

title: Failed ATM, UPI & IMPS Transactions: Auto-Reversal TAT and ₹100/Day Penalty
summary: Under RBI Master Circular DPSS.CO.PD No.629/02.01.014/2019-20 (Harmonisation of Turnaround Time - TAT), banks must auto-reverse failed digital transactions within statutory timelines or pay ₹100 per day compensation directly to the citizen.
documents_needed: Transaction reference number (UPI UTR, ATM receipt, or IMPS reference)

steps.title: Check Statutory Turnaround Time (TAT)
steps.detail: ATM cash withdrawal failure auto-reversal deadline is T + 5 calendar days. UPI and IMPS transfer failure deadline is T + 1 calendar day.

steps.title: Statutory ₹100/Day Penalty Compensation
steps.detail: If the bank fails to reverse the debited amount within the prescribed TAT, the bank is legally obligated to credit ₹100 per day of delay to your account automatically.

steps.title: Lodge Complaint with Your Bank
steps.detail: If the auto-reversal does not happen within TAT, lodge a complaint with your bank's customer care or net banking grievance portal and save the ticket number.

steps.title: Escalate to RBI Banking Ombudsman
steps.detail: If the bank does not resolve the issue or pay compensation within 30 days, file an online complaint at the RBI Complaint Management System (cms.rbi.org.in).

warnings.title: Keep UTR / Transaction Reference Safe
warnings.message: Do not delete SMS or transaction receipts; the unique transaction reference is required for Ombudsman claims.

source.name: Reserve Bank of India - Master Direction on Harmonisation of TAT

title: Aadhaar Cross-Limit Update Exception Appeal (Name, DOB, Gender Limits Exhausted)
summary: UIDAI enforces lifetime update limits: Name (twice), Gender (once), Date of Birth (once for +/- 3 years range). If exhausted, changes can only be approved through the Regional Office exception workflow with a Gazette Notification or Municipal Birth Certificate.
documents_needed: Municipal Birth Certificate (mandatory for Date of Birth cross-limit)
Central or State Gazette Notification (mandatory for Name cross-limit beyond 2 times)
14-digit Enrolment ID (EID) update slip from Aadhaar Seva Kendra

steps.title: Visit Aadhaar Seva Kendra for Initial Enrolment
steps.detail: Visit an authorized Aadhaar center, submit the update request, pay ₹50, and obtain the 14-digit EID slip (the portal will reject it initially due to cross-limit).

steps.title: Obtain Mandatory Statutory Documents
steps.detail: For DOB cross-limit, obtain an official Municipal Birth Certificate. For Name cross-limit, publish a name change notice in the official Government Gazette.

steps.title: Draft Exception Request Letter
steps.detail: Write a formal letter to the UIDAI Regional Office explaining the genuine reason for exceeding the limit, quoting your 12-digit Aadhaar and 14-digit EID numbers.

steps.title: Submit to UIDAI Regional Office for Approval
steps.detail: Email or submit the documents to your jurisdictional UIDAI Regional Office. After verification, the Regional Office approves the cross-limit request on the backend.

warnings.title: Affidavits Not Accepted for Cross-Limit
warnings.message: Notarized affidavits are strictly not accepted for cross-limit updates; only Gazette notifications or Municipal Birth Certificates are valid.

source.name: UIDAI Standard Operating Procedure for Cross-Limit Updates
